title: Money & currency
body:
Portugal uses the euro (EUR). Cards (Visa, Amex, Mastercard/Maestro) are widely accepted, and ATMs are everywhere — you'll rarely need much cash beyond small vendors like Ginjinha stalls.

At airport and tourist-area ATMs, always choose to be charged in euros, not dollars, when prompted — accepting the ATM's own currency conversion (DCC) typically adds a 10%+ markup over your card's own exchange rate.

title: Budget & daily costs
intro: Rough per-person estimates in EUR against the mid-range ($75–150/day) target. Perishable figures are individually sourced below; treat this as a planning range, not a quote.

items.label: Lodging, per night (mid-range)
items.note: Lisbon and Porto mid-range hotel/apartment rates run comparably; treat as a planning range, not a quote.

items.label: Food & drink, per day
items.note: A francesinha or sit-down lunch runs €10-20; a pastel de nata is ≈€1.50. Reservations-level dinners push this higher.

items.label: Local transport, per day
items.note: Metro/tram zapping fares in Lisbon and Porto; day passes cost more but pay off on sightseeing-heavy days.

items.label: Sights & activities, per day
items.note: Belém Tower €15, Jerónimos €18, São Jorge Castle €17, Pena Palace €20, Regaleira €20, Lello ≈€10-16 (unconfirmed tiers), Clérigos €10 — spread across the trip, not all in one day.

items.label: Flights — round trip, into Lisbon / home from Porto
items.note: TAP Air Portugal flies EWR direct to both LIS and OPO — an open-jaw ticket avoids backtracking. ⚠ airfare is dynamic; this is a planning range, not a quote.

items.label: Lisbon–Porto Alfa Pendular train, one-way
items.note: ⚠ cp.pt blocks automated fare verification — aggregator estimates put 2nd class around €25–34; confirm at booking.

items.label: Sintra 24h bus pass (lines 434/435)
items.note: €10.96 confirmed on Parques de Sintra's own ticketing platform — covers the palace shuttle buses, not train fare or monument tickets.
